title: A second mother goes (1882)
hookLine: a conversation goes quiet when you walk in; Thérèse overhears that Pauline, her second mother, is leaving
tomorrow: sick and scared, she turns toward a statue. and then?

cards: A conversation in the kitchen goes quiet the second you walk in. Everyone suddenly busy with the dishes. Something is being decided, and not with you.

Thérèse, still a girl, overhears a conversation like that. Pauline, the sister she chose as her second mother, is going to leave home and enter Carmel, the enclosed convent in town. Nobody has told her yet.
She finds out by accident. And what happens next, in the middle of that hurt, surprises even her.

teach.b: First, the overhearing. Thérèse writes that it hurt terribly. She hadn't understood what it would mean: her sister behind a grille, seen only at visiting times.
Pauline sat with her and explained the life of Carmel, and as she listened, Thérèse felt that she too was called there. Not to follow Pauline, she insists, but for God alone.
She even told the prioress, who believed her but said she was too young. Here's one to tell a friend: the same news that broke her heart planted her own vocation. Then the parting.
Pauline entered, and the visits were hard.

teach.h: THE LAST FEW MINUTES, IN TEARS.
teach.b: Thérèse got only the last few minutes, and spent them in tears. Then the illness.
Not long after, she fell strangely ill: headaches at first, then trembling, terror, frightening things she seemed to see. Her family nursed her and prayed; her father was full of worry.

Looking back, she says she believed the devil had a hand in it. She doesn't pretend to be brave on the page. A child still grieving one mother lost a second, and for a while her body and mind gave way.

how: Carmelite nuns live an enclosed life of prayer; families visit them in a parlor, traditionally through a grille.

games.q: what does “a second mother goes” mean?
o: her mother remarrying after a long wait
a nun moving to a convent in another country
losing the sister she'd chosen as a mother

games.q: your little brother hears from a cousin, not from you, that you're moving out after graduation. he's furious. what does Thérèse's story say went wrong?
o: finding out by accident made it sharper; he needed it from you.
nothing; he'd be upset either way, so how he heard doesn't matter.
nothing; he's too young to be told until it actually happens.
games.why: Thérèse learned of Pauline's plan by chance, and it hurt terribly. then Pauline sat with her and explained the life she was choosing.

practice: Bring to mind one person who feels left behind right now, by a move, a breakup, a friend who drifted. Send them one line that asks nothing back. If you pray, you can say their name to God as it sends.

wordCard.voice: A second mother goes. Pauline's entry into Carmel, and the loss Thérèse felt all over again.

orig.note: Hebrew for Carmel, the biblical mountain the Carmelite order is named for.

carryVoice: The line to keep: left again, because a second loss can reopen the first. Go gently.
